entries.desc: The runtime artifact registry exports explicit entries for current and legacy Koala runtime logs/cache paths, including their ignore patterns and repair behavior.

evidence.note: verification freshness smoke asserts the runtime registry exports current and legacy activity paths as non-material metadata

entries.desc: The registry does not classify .koala/story artifacts, source files, requirements docs, package manifests, or koala.config.json as runtime artifacts.

evidence.note: verification freshness smoke keeps source, package, config, fixture, and requirements files material while excluding only registry runtime artifacts

entries.desc: A future consumer cannot satisfy tests by hardcoding only .koala/activity.jsonl while omitting legacy activity and runtime/cache paths from the registry.

evidence.note: smoke covers both .koala/activity.jsonl and docs/story/activity.jsonl so consumers cannot satisfy coverage by hardcoding only one runtime path

entries.desc: currentMaterialHash and checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit ignore runtime artifacts from the registry, so tracked .koala/activity.jsonl changes keep evidence covered.

evidence.note: materialHash-backed freshness stays covered when tracked .koala/activity.jsonl changes because currentMaterialHash excludes registry runtime artifacts

entries.desc: baseline risk uses the registry to classify runtime artifacts as volatile instead of material dirty paths.

evidence.note: baseline-risk smoke hides .omx runtime residue while still surfacing material user edits before INIT_CHECK

entries.desc: Material files such as packages/main/src/core/verification.ts, package-lock.json, koala.config.json, and docs/requirements remain material and still stale evidence when changed.

evidence.note: real source, package, config, fixture, and requirements files still stale evidence after material changes

entries.desc: A tracked legacy docs/story/activity.jsonl change is also ignored for material freshness, preventing old storage migrations from reintroducing the stale loop.

evidence.note: tracked legacy docs/story/activity.jsonl also remains metadata-only for freshness and coverage reporting

entries.desc: koala init merges missing runtime artifact ignore patterns into an existing .gitignore while preserving existing user content.

evidence.note: entrypoints verification covers merging missing runtime ignore lines into an existing .gitignore under a managed block

entries.desc: koala doctor reports tracked runtime artifacts with a concrete git rm --cached repair hint.

evidence.note: validation protocol smoke makes doctor report tracked .koala/activity.jsonl with a concrete git rm --cached repair command

entries.desc: If all required ignore patterns are already present, koala init leaves .gitignore unchanged except for normal init output.

evidence.note: entrypoints verification keeps an existing .gitignore byte-for-byte unchanged when all required runtime ignores are already present

entries.desc: doctor does not mutate git tracking without --repair, and doctor --repair only untracks registered runtime artifacts rather than broad .koala/story evidence.

evidence.note: doctor --repair untracks only registry-approved runtime artifacts and leaves .koala/story evidence tracked

entries.desc: npm run test:verification-freshness passes and explicitly proves runtime artifacts do not stale materialHash-backed evidence.

evidence.note: verification freshness smoke proves runtime artifacts do not stale materialHash-backed evidence even when the runtime file is tracked

entries.desc: npm run test:entrypoints passes and covers init .gitignore merge behavior for existing projects.

evidence.note: entrypoints verification covers existing-project .gitignore merge and no-churn behavior

entries.desc: The freshness smoke still proves real material paths are stale, so the runtime exclusion is not overly broad.

evidence.note: the smoke still marks source, package, config, fixture, and requirements paths stale so the exclusion stays narrow

entries.desc: A tracked runtime artifact scenario is tested, not just an ignored untracked file scenario.

evidence.note: tracked runtime artifact coverage is explicit in the smoke, not just an ignored-untracked-file scenario
